transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-24
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO - Tidal Tech), Sofia Morales (ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Head of Product)
Links shared: Deck: https://shorturl.at/rtX3, Security pack: https://redwood.docs/security-pack, Pricing/TCO draft: https://shorturl.at/tco2027

Summary (auto): quick discovery for model selection and deployment mode. Customer cares about multilingual support, long-context (up to ~100k tokens on doc ingestion), tool/function calling for retrieval and API calls, and options for hosted vs dedicated vs private w/ SOC2/KMS. Agreed next step: share pricing/TCO, schedule deep technical bench with SE; customer to share prompts.

Topics: model families (open models), context lengths (8k/32k/128k/100k), multilingual, tool-calling/function-calling, privacy/VPC/KMS, latency vs cost, POC sizing

[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone — thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick intros?
[00:12] Raj (CTO): Hey, Raj here, I run infra/ML. Sofia and Liam are on as well.
[00:18] Sofia (ML): Hi, Sofia, ML engineer working on retrieval and summarization pipelines.
[00:22] Liam (Product): Liam, head of product, focused on UX and latency targets.
[00:26] Jordan: Great. Maya from our SE team will cover technical bits after I run through goals.
[00:30] Maya (SE): hi all.

[00:33] Jordan: Quick context: Tidal Tech builds an enterprise knowledge assistant for customer support and contract summarization; main asks today are picking model(s) and deployment mode — hosted vs dedicated vs private — especially around long documents and multilingual responses. want to understand your constraints.

[01:05] Raj: High level: we ingest legal/contract docs, sometimes 50-100 pages, need to answer complex queries across docs. we also have customers in EMEA and LATAM, so multi-lang support is required. Latency target for interactive UI is sub-600ms token latency ideally, but we can tolerate up to 1.2s for some ops. Cost is important, we have budget constraints. Security: SOC2 required, SSO SAML, and KMS for keys — for some customers we'll need VPC/private.

[01:45] Maya: Got it. on model side, are you looking at open models only or considering hosted proprietary options?

[01:52] Raj: Prefer open models for cost and control, but we need function calling/tool-calling too — like calling a retrieval API, database queries, and limited actions. Also want reproducibility and version pinning.

[02:10] Jordan: Typical. Redwood supports hosted API for faster onboarding, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem. For model choices, we recommend evaluating model families that support tool/function calling and have long-context variants. Examples: Llama-3 style family (32k/70k variants), Mistral/ Mistral-large, Falcon-X (if you need high throughput), and some of the emerging 100k-context models for heavy documents. we can surface Redwood-verified perf profiles.

[02:44] Sofia: Do these open models reliably support function-calling, or is that more an LLM-provider feature? we need structured JSON outputs too.

[02:52] Maya: function-calling itself is an interface layer — we support structured output and function/tool invocation patterns in the Redwood API. it's up to model capability how deterministic the outputs are, but we use schema-guided prompting and lightweight reranking to improve structure. also we do streaming + function-calls so you can pipe partial responses to downstream services.

[03:20] Liam: for context length, we have some cases that are effectively 80-120k tokens if you include multiple contracts. we were hoping for a single-pass context but are open to retrieval + chunking. any recommendations?

[03:36] Maya: For docs that large, two common approaches: 1) use a long-context model (100k context models exist but are heavier/costlier and sometimes experimental), or 2) retrieval-augmented generation with dense embeddings and chunked contexts — often paired with KV-caching and prefix caching to reduce tokens for repeated queries. For interactive latency, RA strategies plus shorter model contexts (32k) can be more predictable and cheaper.

[04:10] Raj: We're leaning toward a mixed approach. want to keep an experimental long-context path for deep legal queries but default to retrieval for UI. Also concerned about hallucinations; how does Redwood help monitor/regressions?

[04:26] Jordan: Redwood Optimize and Console give quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals — you can set regression alerts, track per-prompt quality metrics, and compare model/quantization changes. we can set up eval harnesses during the POC.

[04:45] Sofia: On multilingual: we need Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Portuguese Brazilian, and occasional Japanese. Are open models good at multilingual out-of-the-box?

[04:58] Maya: Some families have stronger multilingual capabilities (e.g., Llama-3 variants and certain Mistral weights); others degrade. We recommend performing language-specific evals — small sample prompts in each language — and we'll surface model rankings for each language. also embeddings for semantic search: we can run multilingual embeddings or use language-specific embedding models depending on precision needs.

[05:30] Raj: On the deployment mode: if we go hosted, is data ever persisted on shared infra? we need to know about isolation and encryption.

[05:40] Jordan: Hosted API is isolated per-tenant logical isolation, SOC2, at-rest encryption, and optional customer-managed keys for certain plans. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with stronger isolation and throughput SLAs. Private provides a customer VPC control plane — you control the network and can use your KMS/HSM. We'll send the security pack that maps features to compliance controls.

[06:05] Liam: What about latency differences? if we need sub-600ms, is hosted viable?

[06:12] Maya: It depends on model size and region. For smaller open models (quantized 8-bit or bfloat paths) you can get sub-600ms token latency in hosted for moderate loads. If you need guaranteed low tail latencies at scale, Dedicated with reserved GPUs and placement in region is recommended — plus we can pin models and kernels for predictable perf.

[06:40] Raj: We also want to run offline batch summarizations overnight for 10k docs — anything special to consider?

[06:47] Maya: Batch jobs map well to Dedicated or Private where you can schedule capacity and not impact interactive traffic. Redwood's runtime supports batching and auto-scaling policies to optimize unit cost for large batches.

[07:00] Jordan: Can you share a rough QPS/throughput expectation?

[07:05] Raj: For interactive UI peak we're thinking 8-12 RPS with spikes to 20 during business hours, and nightly batch throughput that's heavy but can be scheduled.

[07:14] Maya: That helps POC sizing. We'll run a capacity plan: for 12 RPS interactive with 32k context models and occasional 100k jobs, we'd recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale + burst to hosted as fallback if you want strict SLOs.

[07:36] Sofia: On costs — quantization? we plan to use 4-bit or 8-bit quantized models if accuracy permits. How does Redwood handle quantized weights and model variants?

[07:45] Maya: Redwood supports quantized execution paths and will recommend quantization profiles based on workload. Optimize can suggest whether 4-bit is acceptable vs 8-bit, and we track quality regressions per prompt. The runtime picks kernels appropriate for quantized models; some older kernels may not support extreme context lengths.

[08:05] Liam: Any specific examples of customers doing long-context legal workflows?

[08:11] Jordan: Yes, a few mid-market legal SaaS customers. They used a hybrid approach: embeddings + retrieval for most UI queries, and a long-context model for deep case analysis behind a slower workflow. we can anonymize a case study after NDA.

[08:30] Raj: For POC, we'd like to evaluate three models: a robust 32k open model, a high-throughput smaller model for cost-sensitive tasks, and a long-context experimental model for deep queries. can Redwood help pick specific checkpoints and pins?

[08:46] Maya: Absolutely. We'll propose candidates (e.g., Llama-3 32k rev, Mistral-large, and a 100k-context variant) and provide perf/latency/cost tradeoffs. we'll also recommend embedding model pairings and reranking thresholds.

[09:05] Jordan: also wanna call out that tool-calling patterns: do you need guaranteed transactional calls? like when agent triggers an API to change state?

[09:14] Sofia: yes, eventually. for now most tool calls are read-only (DB queries, retrieval). but roadmap includes write-actions where we need stronger guarantees.

[09:24] Maya: For transactional writes we recommend designing idempotent APIs and using function-calling with explicit confirmations; Redwood supports structured function-calls and logging hooks so you can audit calls. Private/VPC gives additional network controls for secure outbound webhooks.

[09:44] Liam: On observability, we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model and per route. Is that in the console?

[09:52] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route and per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. You can also wire alerts to Slack.

[10:05] Raj: Security questions — we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs forwarded to SIEM, and KMS integration. are these possible on hosted?

[10:14] Jordan: SSO and RBAC are available for hosted plans. Audit logs and log-forwarding are available for Dedicated and Private with longer retention as an add-on. Customer-managed KMS is primarily available on Dedicated/Private; hosted may offer bring-your-own-key on enterprise tiers. we'll map exact items in the security pack.

[10:35] Sofia: If we go Private, what's the install footprint? any on-prem options?

[10:40] Maya: Private can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem clusters with our control-plane integration. footprint depends on model sizes and desired throughput; for example, a pool to handle your interactive load plus batch will need N GPUs — we'll size it after initial benchmarks.

[11:00] Jordan: let's talk POC timeline — what are you aiming for?

[11:04] Raj: We want a 6-week POC: week 1-2 baseline + data prep, week 3 run benchmarks and latency tests, week 4-5 iterate on prompts and reranking, week 6 evaluate results and go/no-go.

[11:18] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a POC plan and required artifacts.

[11:25] Sofia: On data retention — do you store user prompts and responses? how long? we need to be able to set retention policies per customer.

[11:34] Maya: You can configure retention policies and ingestion behaviors. For Hosted we default to short retention but can enable longer retention for analytics. Dedicated/Private gives you more control and local logs.

[11:50] Raj: Some micro-questions from our infra team: does Redwood's runtime support KV cache for decoder-side caching across sessions? we have lots of repeated prefixes.

[11:59] Maya: Yes, runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; this helps repeated conversational contexts and reduces compute. We also have intelligent routing and cache-aware batching to reduce token costs.

[12:20] Jordan: any specific latency SLA numbers you're targeting for POC?

[12:24] Liam: sub-600ms  p99 ideally for interactive queries. we know p50 will be lower.

[12:32] Maya: We'll instrument p50/p95/p99. For p99 under 600ms you'd likely need Dedicated with pinned models and kernels; hosted can sometimes get close but not guaranteed.

[12:50] Raj: For the evaluation prompts, we'll include long multi-doc queries, short chatty customer messages, and API-triggering flows.

[13:00] Jordan: Perfect. We'll need sample prompts and a sample of the document corpus — roughly how big?

[13:06] Sofia: We'll provide 10-20 representative long docs and a set of 100 prompts across languages. Also a smaller set for transactional tool-calls.

[13:18] Jordan: Great. Maya — anything tech-deep we should call out now or save for SE deep dive?

[13:25] Maya: I'd like to run through kernel selection, quantization tradeoffs, and a quick perf checklist in the deep dive. For now, I want to capture that you care about: 1) 100k-class long-context options, 2) multilingual accuracy, 3) function-calling reliability, 4) predictable latency at p99.

[13:45] Raj: Yep. Also curious about fallback policies — if dedicated pool is saturated can Redwood route to hosted as fallback?

[13:50] Maya: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity. Policies can be configured by latency, cost, region, or tier. That said, fallback model may have different perf/accuracy characteristics, so plan accordingly.

[14:10] Liam: About pricing — do you have ballpark numbers for quantized 32k vs long-context 100k models?

[14:16] Jordan: We'll send spreadsheet with modeled TCO including tokens, fixed reserved capacity costs for Dedicated, and delta for long-context models (they cost more per token and compute). Also include cost for Private deployment (license + infra).

[14:36] Raj: On compliance: we might have a few EU customers that require data residency. Is regional hosting available?

[14:43] Jordan: Yes, we have regional options in EU and NA and can map data residency requirements. Private/VPC is the stronger control if you need strict residency.

[14:55] Sofia: Anything around model updates and rollouts? we want ability to pin versions and do canary tests.

[15:02] Maya: Redwood supports rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies and version pinning. Console gives you per-model dashboards for that.

[15:18] Jordan: Ok let's do a quick recap of agreed next steps.

[15:22] Raj: sure.

[15:25] Jordan: 1) Redwood to send pricing/TCO spreadsheet and security pack. 2) SE to schedule a 90-min technical deep dive next week for kernel/quantization/perf. 3) Tidal to upload sample docs and 100 prompts for multilingual evaluation. 4) We'll propose 3 model checkpoints for POC and a capacity plan.

[15:40] Liam: sounds good.

[15:44] Raj: one more question — do you support streaming partial tokens to front-end for perceived latency improvements?

[15:50] Maya: Yes, streaming responses are supported and you can stream interim tokens while function-calls can be emitted separately. It's often used to improve perceived latency.

[16:05] Sofia: Are there any gotchas with embeddings for multilingual retrieval? do we need to normalize text?

[16:12] Maya: Good question. tokenization and normalization matter; we recommend language-specific pre-processing in some cases and running evals to pick the embedding model. We can run a small multi-language similarity test in the POC.

[16:30] Jordan: Ok team — we'll action the artifacts. Any final questions?

[16:36] Raj: Not from me, thanks.

[16:40] Sofia: quick note — we'll likely want a Private evaluation if security checks are strict; might request a short on-prem pilot.

[16:48] Jordan: Noted — we'll include Private sizing and on-prem options in the POC doc.

[16:55] Liam: Thanks everyone.

[17:00] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and schedule the SE deep dive.

[17:06] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcribed, occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" in one spot, product names sometimes shortened), speaker labels preserved where possible.

Action items recap: Jordan to send pricing/TCO + security pack; Maya to schedule deep tech dive and share benchmark checklist; Raj to upload corpus and prompts.

End of transcript.
